Two friends. Same college, same office, same salary. At sixty, one has crores. The other, lakhs.
Meet Arun and Karthik. Both twenty five, both earning fifty thousand a month in Chennai.
Arun starts a ten thousand rupee SIP in a Nifty index fund. Every month. No skipping.
Karthik says, I'll start later. First the bike EMI. Then a new phone. Then the wedding. Then the car.
At forty five, Karthik finally starts the same ten thousand rupee SIP.
Both stop at sixty. Arun put in forty two lakh. Karthik put in eighteen lakh.
At twelve percent a year, close to the Nifty fifty's long run average, Arun ends with five point five crore. Karthik, forty seven lakh.
Arun invested two times more. He ended with eleven times more. Those extra twenty years did the heavy lifting.
Honest note. Returns are not guaranteed, and inflation is real. In today's money, Arun's pile is about seventy two lakh. Karthik's, about six lakh.
Which friend are you? Tag your Karthik. Save this, and follow money in cloud.
